markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged readings, one from a SERIES setup and one from a PARALLEL setup, with the bulb number and brightness (or current) from their Investigation Record.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine Record rows, e.g. series 3 bulbs about 11% each (2 cells) and parallel 3 bulbs 100% each; exact numbers must be consistent with the student's own rows.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('series is dimmer') with no logged numbers, or numbers that do not appear in their Record.

markingScheme.criterion: States the comparison: as bulbs were added in series each bulb got dimmer (the cell's push is shared), whereas in parallel each bulb stayed as bright.
markingScheme.accept: Any clear statement that series bulbs were dimmer than parallel bulbs for the same number of bulbs and cells, or that brightness fell in series but not in parallel.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only that the circuits were 'different' or that parallel was 'better' with no mention of brightness.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why: in a series circuit there is one path so the cell's push (energy) is shared between all the bulbs; in a parallel circuit each bulb has its own branch straight to the cell so each gets the full push.
markingScheme.accept: Any valid wording of 'shared between bulbs in series' and 'each has its own path / gets the full voltage in parallel'; the word voltage is not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the comparison ('parallel is brighter because it is parallel') with no mention of one path versus separate paths.

markingScheme.criterion: States what happens when one bulb breaks in each type: in SERIES all the other lights go out; in PARALLEL the other lights stay on.
markingScheme.accept: Both outcomes stated correctly, in any wording.
markingScheme.insufficient: Only one of the two circuit types described, or the outcomes swapped.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why: a series circuit has a single loop, so a broken bulb breaks the only loop and the current stops everywhere; in parallel each bulb is on its own loop, so breaking one loop does not stop current in the others.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct reference to one path/loop versus separate paths/branches/loops.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'because it is parallel' with no reference to loops, paths or branches.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives ONE other valid advantage of parallel wiring (for example: every lamp gets full brightness, each lamp can have its own switch, a faulty lamp is easy to find, or other lights are not affected by a fault).
markingScheme.accept: Any one correct extra advantage; 'drains the battery faster' is not an advantage and does not earn the mark.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating that the other lights stay on (already credited in the first point).
